But if len(active) != 1, ok is already False... but the code still executes the merged check with active[0] — if active is empty, IndexError. That's a real robustness bug but... the verdict criteria: "an edit with a bug or that breaks existing behaviour." A crash in a failure path is arguably a bug. 12. The item says "replace the whole of scripts/verify_merge.py" — the file doesn't exist in scripts/ (only merge_duplicates.py and stock_report.py). Creating it is fine; "replace the whole of" a nonexistent file = create. Not a rejection reason.

13. One more check: does the script verify "no records were deleted"? It prints total records but doesn't verify count against anything. It can't know the original count. The plan step P2 says verify "no records were deleted" — the script prints total but doesn't check. Hmm, it can't check without a baseline. It's a partial fulfillment. Not necessarily wrong.

A crash instead of a clean FAILED report in a failure scenario — the script would still terminate with an error, so verification would still be seen as failed.
